title.narrative: Justice, Rule of Law, Human Rights, Institutions "JEDI 2"

description.narrative: The project started on 1 March 2023 and will end on 28 February 2027. The project is implemented through a three-fold approach to achieve its overall objective. Firstly, it seeks to empower Tunisian citizens to pursue their rights to access justice (Outcome I) by increasing their awareness about administrative justice, the related rights and means to access them (Output 1), and providing information to local stakeholders to support citizens in their demand of justice (Output 2). Secondly, the project fosters an enabling and more efficient environment for the administrative justice (Outcome II), equipping the Administrative Tribunal (AT) with the tools and skills to provide better access to information to citizens (Output 3), improve judicial services (Output 4), and enhance case management (Output 5). Thirdly, the project aims at enhancing human and fundamental rights (Outcome III) by making legal information on justice available to promote good governance (Output 6) and utilizing it to engage citizens in public conversations at the local and national level (Output 7). The combination of these work streams will eventually improve justice services and raise citizens’ awareness on their fundamental rights, thus contributing to strengthening the rule of law (Impact).

policy-marker.narrative: Gender equality is an fundamental aspect of DRI’s mission to promote democracy. In our view, equality is an integral part of democracy, including for all genders, religious, ethnic, and socio-economic groups, and people of different ages and abilities. DRI commits to a gender-sensitive approach and to mainstreaming gender issues in all aspects of our projects. In line with UN Resolution 132514 and SDG 5, and to ensure that DRI’s projects are designed, implemented and evaluated in a gender-sensitive manner, we have introduced a gender and diversity policy and a gender mainstreaming tool which is applied across our offices worldwide. This activity will therefore place special emphasis on gender and diversity by ensuring the equal participation of women and vulnerable groups in project activities, and, whenever relevant to the context, emphasizing gender issues.

This second phase of the project aims to continue and build on the efforts started under the JEDI I project, with the support provided by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Netherlands, to raise awareness of rights with the support of civil society organization (CSO) partners, while ensuring continuity of support to institutions guaranteeing rights and freedoms in this exceptional context. DRI use a people-centred justice approach that relies on perspectives, needs, strengths, and expectations of justice users to improve the quality of justice and reduce barriers to service delivery. It is an approach designed to fill the gaps of traditional, institution-focused programming by bridging the gap between citizens and state institutions providing services to citizens. The project will mainly target citizens, CSOs, judges and court personnel, using a dual approach combining the capacity building of partners to ultimately improve citizens' knowledge of rights and means to access justice, as well as the support to institutions of justice through organisational development to improve their effectiveness in service delivery.

description.narrative: This indicator assesses the percentage by which awareness or knowledge about the rights and procedures related to administrative justice has increased over the project timeframe. To measure this, a baseline and endline surveys will be conducted to gauge the extent of public knowledge regarding administrative justice, rights and procedures.

title.narrative: % of citizen seeking justice

description.narrative: Ratio of # individuals engaged / # individuals interested in administrative justice The number of citizens interested measures the level of interest of citizens in the various activities and events of the project, it is equal to: #individuals visiting tents, mega events and justibus + # of interactions on social media ( share, comment, reaction..)+ # of access to the media center+ participants in events and initiatives focused on vulnerable populations. The number of engaged citizens quantifies the level of engagement of citizens in the various project activities and events. It is equal to: The number of individuals consulting experts at the tents, Justibus, and mega events + # of individuals consulting the references of the media center + # of downloads from the media center + # messages and discussions related to administrative justice received on social media platforms

title.narrative: II.4 Output 4 : Accessibility to and quality of judicial services is improved
% of user satisfaction (with people who visit the court with pre and post evaluation)

description.narrative: This indicator quantifies the improvement in satisfaction levels among individuals who visit the Regional chambers, comparing their experiences before and after the implementation of the "Marhaba" label certification. This measurement assesses the effectiveness of the certification process in enhancing the quality of court reception and services by comparing user satisfaction levels before the certification (pre-evaluation) and after the certification (post-evaluation). A higher percentage indicates a positive impact on user satisfaction resulting from the certification initiative.
